app: Anicca iOS (evidence read 2026-11-16: canonical checkout Daisuke134/anicca, branch claude/living-home-paywall-2026-11-15, HEAD a553a6e42; Services/PushTokenService.swift and AppDelegate.swift read in full, PushTokenServiceTests.swift read in full, entitlements and Config.swift read. Registration IS requested whenever authorized: AppDelegate.registerForRemoteIfAuthorized runs at launch and again on applicationDidBecomeActive, and registerForRemoteNotifications is also called from the onboarding permission step and from Settings. didRegisterForRemoteNotificationsWithDeviceToken forwards unconditionally to PushTokenService.register on every callback -- no local token cache suppresses the forward, and the token itself is never stored on device (only the boolean flag com.anicca.apnsTokenRegistered). register() POSTs {token, platform: ios} to /mobile/push/token with device-id, x-timezone and x-lang headers; on 2xx it reads remoteProblemNudgesEnabled and only then sets the registered flag and cancels local Problem notifications, otherwise it unmarks and reschedules local delivery; on non-2xx, non-HTTP or network error it restores local Problem notifications. Outcomes are measured via notificationRegistrationResult with result registered / failed / invalid_device_token / response_unrecognized, source, server_status_code and error_code. BUT: register() rejects any token whose hex length is not exactly 64 (invalid_device_token). The request body carries NO environment field and no lifecycle / owner / environment-mapping decision is recorded in the repo, so how the server keys, replaces or separates tokens is unrecorded and the backend itself is outside this checkout (unverified, not asserted absent). didFailToRegister tracks the failure and calls markUnregistered but does NOT restore local Problem notifications, while the POST-failure path does -- and its own comment calls the design remote-only with no local fallback, contradicting the fallback the register() path maintains. Retry exists only implicitly: the next launch or foregrounding re-registers and re-forwards. No deregistration exists anywhere: grep for unregister / deregister / deleteToken across the tree is 0, markUnregistered only flips the local flag, and sign-out, the account-deletion wipe and permission loss never tell the server to retire the token. No token-coverage or stale-token-age measurement is recorded. aps-environment is production in aniccaios.entitlements and aniccaiosDistribution.entitlements and development in aniccaiosDebug.entitlements.)
